name: How do older Salt Lake City homes affect under-cabinet lighting installations?

mainEntity.name: How do older Salt Lake City homes affect under-cabinet lighting installations?

acceptedAnswer.text: Homeowners in Salt Lake City historic neighborhoods like The Avenues, Harvard-Yale, or Capitol Hill often face unique structural constraints when remodeling older kitchens. Older lath-and-plaster walls, shallow original cabinetry, and ungrounded electrical circuits require careful investigation before adding modern low-voltage systems. In these homes, general contractors often run new dedicated circuits from the main panel through floor joists or basements to avoid damaging historic plaster. Using shallow-depth, high-output LED tape channels ensures modern brightness fits within historic cabinet frames without altering original architectural millwork.
acceptedAnswer.description: Older homes with lath-and-plaster walls or original cabinetry often require new dedicated circuit runs from below and shallow fixture profiles to preserve historic trim.
